name: corsixth
desc: Open source clone of Theme Hospital
why: An open source Theme Hospital reimplementation whose simulation of queues and staff is a joy to tinker with and reverse-engineered from the original.

brief.what_it_is: CorsixTH is an open source reimplementation of Theme Hospital, the 1997 Bullfrog hospital management sim. It runs the game on modern Windows, macOS, Linux and BSD, and adds high-resolution display, zooming, UI scaling, subtitles, more than 20 languages, a built-in map editor, custom levels and campaigns, and custom music playback. It needs the original game's graphics, sound and data files, which you supply from an existing copy. The output is the playable game itself.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says it is a reimplementation that faithfully recreates the original while adding support for modern operating systems, high resolutions and much more. Its stated goal is to keep Theme Hospital playable on current systems.
brief.how_it_works: Most of the game logic is written in Lua, with the rest in C++. The project uses the original game's assets (graphics, sound and other data) rather than replacing them, so a legitimate copy of the original is required. The README does not describe the reverse-engineering or simulation internals in detail.
brief.install_notes: Install from a packaged build: a Windows or macOS installer and a Linux AppImage on the releases page, or a distro package under the name corsixth or corsix-th, a Flatpak from Flathub (com.corsixth.corsixth), a Snap from Snapcraft, or an unofficial Anylinux AppImage from Pkgforge. You also need the original game data, from an original CD or a download from GOG.com or EA. The README points to the wiki Getting Started page for first-run detail. No commands are shown in the README.
brief.standout: It is a full-featured free rebuild of a 1997 sim that still needs the original data files, and it adds modern conveniences such as zoom, 4K support, a map editor and the option to build rooms while paused. The brew scout note calls the queue and staff simulation a joy to tinker with and says it was reverse-engineered, but the README itself does not say that, so treat those claims as unverified.
brief.status: Likely maintained, but the date is unknown. The README shows a release badge and CI badges for Linux, Windows and AppVeyor, and it recruits contributors and links to an open issue tracker with Good First Issue labels. I did not check the releases page or commit history for a date.
brief.caveats: Missing features, per the README: multiplayer/LAN, AI hospitals, rats (rat holes are present but not rats or the bonus rat level), vomit waves, and the win-level video/letter. Pregnancy, Alien DNA and female Fractured Bones patients lack a complete graphics set and may cause anomalies if regular spawning is enabled. Some objects may glitch with walls. It needs the original game's data files, so it is not standalone. The README does not state a license, so licensing is unknown from the page I read.
